pairs: Fili mi,
My son,
attende ad sapientiam meam,
pay attention to my wisdom,
et prudentiæ meæ inclina aurem tuam:
and incline your ear to my prudence,
ut custodias cogitationes,
so that you may guard your thinking,
et disciplinam labia tua conservent.
and so that your lips may preserve discipline.
Ne attendas fallaciæ mulieris;
Do not pay attention to the deceit of a woman.
favus enim distillans labia meretricis,
For the lips of a loose woman are like a dripping honeycomb,
et nitidius oleo guttur ejus:
and her voice is smoother than oil.
novissima autem illius amara quasi absinthium,
But in the end, she is as bitter as wormwood,
et acuta quasi gladius biceps.
and as sharp as a two-edged sword.
Pedes ejus descendunt in mortem,
Her feet descend into death,
et ad inferos gressus illius penetrant.
and her steps reach even to Hell.
Per semitam vitæ non ambulant;
They do not walk along the path of life;
vagi sunt gressus ejus et investigabiles.
her steps are wandering and untraceable.
Nunc ergo fili mi,
Therefore, my son,
audi me,
listen to me now,
et ne recedas a verbis oris mei.
and do not withdraw from the words of my mouth.
Longe fac ab ea viam tuam,
Make your way at a distance from her,
et ne appropinques foribus domus ejus.
and do not approach the doors of her house.
Ne des alienis honorem tuum,
Do not give your honor to foreigners,
et annos tuos crudeli:
and your years to the cruel.
ne forte impleantur extranei viribus tuis,
Otherwise, outsiders may be filled with your strength,
et labores tui sint in domo aliena,
and your labors may be in a foreign house,
et gemas in novissimis,
and you may mourn in the end,
quando consumpseris carnes tuas et corpus tuum,
when you will have consumed your flesh and your body.
et dicas:
And so you may say:
Cur detestatus sum disciplinam,
“Why have I detested discipline,
et increpationibus non acquievit cor meum,
and why has my heart not been quieted by correction?
nec audivi vocem docentium me,
And why have I not listened to the voice of those who guided me?
et magistris non inclinavi aurem meam?
And why has my ear not inclined to my teachers?
pene fui in omni malo,
I have almost been with all evil in the midst of the church
in medio ecclesiæ et synagogæ.
and of the assembly.”
Bibe aquam de cisterna tua,
Drink water from your own cistern
et fluenta putei tui;
and from the springs of your own well.
deriventur fontes tui foras,
Let your fountains be diverted far and wide,
et in plateis aquas tuas divide.
and divide your waters in the streets.
Habeto eas solus,
Hold them for yourself alone,
nec sint alieni participes tui.
and do not let strangers be partakers with you.
Sit vena tua benedicta,
Let your spring be blessed,
et lætare cum muliere adolescentiæ tuæ.
and rejoice with the wife of your youth:
Cerva carissima,
a beloved doe
et gratissimus hinnulus:
and most pleasing fawn.
ubera ejus inebrient te in omni tempore;
Let her breasts inebriate you at all times.
in amore ejus delectare jugiter.
Be delighted continually by her love.
Quare seduceris,
Why are you seduced,
fili mi,
my son,
ab aliena,
by a strange woman,
et foveris in sinu alterius?
and why are you kept warm by the bosom of another?
Respicit Dominus vias hominis,
The Lord beholds the ways of man,
et omnes gressus ejus considerat.
and he considers all his steps.
Iniquitates suas capiunt impium,
His own iniquities take hold of the impious,
et funibus peccatorum suorum constringitur.
and he is bound by the cords of his own sins.
Ipse morietur,
He shall die,
quia non habuit disciplinam,
for he has not held to discipline.
et in multitudine stultitiæ suæ decipietur.
And by the multitude of his foolishness, he shall be deceived.
